source.episode_title: One Goat Died. One Was Sent Away. Why Two?
source.anchor_kjv: And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away by the hand of a fit man into the wilderness: And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land not inhabited: and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness.
source.thread: Two goats, one sin offering, pictured in Christ
source.spoken_script: One goat died. One goat lived. Why two? I am Aaron, the high priest. I lived long before Jesus, so watch my goats. The first I killed, to pay for the people's sin. I carried its blood behind the curtain, where God's presence was, and no one else could go. The second I did not kill. I laid both hands on its head, and confessed the people's sins. Then it was sent away alive, into the wilderness. The dead goat could not walk away. The living goat could not pay. Jesus, God's Son, did both. He came "to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself". When He died, the temple curtain tore, "from the top to the bottom". I went in once a year, alone. Through Jesus, the curtain is open. Walk through, to God.

platforms.description:
Leviticus 16:21-22: on the Day of Atonement, Aaron the high priest handled two goats that together made one sin offering. One was killed and its blood carried behind the curtain. The other had the people's sins confessed over it and was sent away alive. Why two? Christians see both halves of one rescue, and Jesus did both.

"And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him away by the hand of a fit man into the wilderness: And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land not inhabited: and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness." (Leviticus 16:21-22, KJV)

When Jesus died, the temple curtain tore from the top to the bottom. Through Jesus, the curtain is open. Walk through, to God.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS
- Anchor quote: matches Leviticus 16:21-22 KJV. No change.
- Title: "Why Two?" gap is true to the text (Lev 16:8-10, one sin offering, v5). Not clickbait.
- Doctrine: the two-halves-and-Jesus-did-both reading is framed as what "Christians see", not as Leviticus's own claim. Good. Curtain tearing top to bottom is Matt 27:51.
- CTA: "Walk through, to God" is an invitation, no fear or gain-loss framing.
- Platform: TikTok/Instagram hooks come first. Fine.
